title: The integral stratum bound
statement:
In the situation of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion],

$$
\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)=0\quad(q>\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2),
$$

Ext taken in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lattice-supported-hom-reduction-tower] to the given $a,L_0,b,M_0$. Use its notation $R_Y,A_{n,Y},Q,N,\overline N_n,N_n,F_n,B_n$ and the quotient transitions. It gives $B_n\in D(\operatorname{Ab})$, $H^q(B_n)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(Q,N_n[q])$ and $\Ext^q_{R_X}(Q,N)\cong H^q(R\varprojlim_nB_n)$ for every $q$.

source.place: Integral targets, support-Hom formula and commuting derived global sections with the derived limit; Stacks Tag 0D6K, label lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim

proof.text: For each $n\ge1$, apply [lem-sfb-lattice-supported-hom-finite-comparison] with $\overline K=\overline N_n=b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$. Step 1 and its three comparison isomorphisms identify $H^q(B_n)$ with $H^qR\Gamma(S,(L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n)\otimes_{A_{n,S}}u^*R\underline\Gamma_{Z,A_n}b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n))$. Clause (2) of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion] therefore gives $H^q(B_n)=0$ for $q>c$, uniformly in $n$, where $c=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+1$. The support functor in this application is in the finite coefficient category.

source.place: Integral targets, the assertion that the reductions have the torsion stratum bound; Torsion targets, last display

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] to the tower $B_n$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ from Step 1. It gives
$$0\longrightarrow R^1\varprojlim_nH^{q-1}(B_n)\longrightarrow H^q(R\varprojlim_nB_n)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_nH^q(B_n)\longrightarrow0.$$
For $q>c+1$, both $q>c$ and $q-1>c$, so Step 2 makes each of the two towers in the end terms the zero tower. Their limit and first derived limit are zero (the zero object has the zero injective resolution), hence the middle group is zero by exactness. Step 1 identifies that group with $\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)$. Since $c+1=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$, this is precisely the claimed bound. No surjectivity or Mittag-Leffler assumption on the cohomology towers is used. If a cohomological dimension is infinite the claimed range is empty, so only the finite-bound case needs this computation.
